q-71532.problem: Suppose $|\,c\,|=18$ and the angle between vectors $c$ and $d$ is $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}.$ Find the scalar projection of $c$ onto $d.$
q-71532.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{d}\,c & =|\,c\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =18\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =18\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-9\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}

q-18374.name: Question 6
q-18374.problem: Let $p=⟨\sqrt{2},1,-1⟩$ and $q=⟨\sqrt{8},-\sqrt{3},1⟩.$ Find the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q.$
q-18374.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{q}\,p & =\frac{p\cdot q}{|\,q\,|} \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{\sqrt{{q}_{x}^{2}+{q}_{y}^{2}+{q}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{8}+1\cdot (-\sqrt{3})+(-1)\cdot 1}{\sqrt{(\sqrt{8})^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{12}} \\  & =\frac{3-\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-237018.name: Question 11
q-237018.problem: Let $a=5i-4j+3k$ and $b=-7i+xj+k.$ Given that the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b$ is zero, find the value of $x.$
q-237018.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =5\cdot (-7)+(-4)\cdot x+3\cdot 1 \\  & =-4x-32.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ -4x-32 & =0 \\ 4x & =-32 \\ x & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$
